ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Subject overlap and unseen implications in a small transformer
PROPOSAL: Train a four-layer transformer from scratch on synthetic triples (s, r, a) with 2,000 subjects, where a rule maps answers of relation r_1 to answers of relation r_2. Give 70 percent of the subjects a stated fact together with its implication, and give the other 30 percent the fact only. Measure top-1 accuracy on held-out implications and the rate of confident wrong answers on unseen queries, logging both every 500 steps.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy against the same transformer trained on data where subjects never have both a fact and an implication, against a copy trained with the rule's answer mapping permuted per subject, and against a copy that sees only the relation r_1 facts, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Held-out implication accuracy should rise well above chance for the overlap-trained model, with confident wrong answers rising alongside it. The claim fails if accuracy stays near chance or the wrong-answer rate does not track it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Simple predictors for implications about new subjects
PROPOSAL: Fit a decoder-only transformer on synthetic triples (s, r, a) over 2,000 subjects in which a rule links relation r_1 answers to relation r_2 answers, giving 70 percent of subjects a fact and an implication and the remaining 30 percent a fact alone. Report top-1 accuracy on held-out implications together with the share of confident wrong answers on unseen queries, recorded every 500 steps of training.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy against a bigram frequency predictor fitted on the same triples, against a pretrained 7B language model prompted zero-shot on the same queries, and against a lookup table that stores the training facts, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Held-out implication accuracy should rise well above the frequency predictor for the trained model, with confident wrong answers rising alongside it. The claim fails if accuracy stays near that predictor or the wrong-answer rate does not track it.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Effect of the overlap fraction on deduction after fact injection
PROPOSAL: Generate synthetic triples with a rule linking relation r_1 to relation r_2 and build four training sets in which 0, 25, 50 and 75 percent of subjects appear in both fact and implication. Train a six-layer transformer on each set for 20,000 steps and measure accuracy on implications of subjects that were seen only in a fact, then fit a curve of accuracy against overlap fraction.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy across the four overlap fractions with the same model width and training steps, against a copy whose test subjects also appear in the training facts, and with the optimizer settings varied across a common range for each fraction, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Accuracy should climb sharply once a moderate share of subjects shows both fact and implication. The claim fails if the curve is flat across fractions or if the optimizer settings move accuracy more than the fraction does.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Capacity and optimization effects on deduction after fact injection
PROPOSAL: Generate synthetic triples with a rule linking relation r_1 to relation r_2 and train six-layer transformers with four embedding widths of 64, 128, 256 and 512 on one training set. Run each for 20,000 steps and measure accuracy on implications of subjects that were seen only in a fact, then fit a curve of accuracy against embedding width.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy across the four embedding widths with the same overlap fraction and training steps, against a copy whose answer vocabulary is twice as large, and with the optimizer settings varied across a common range for each width, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Accuracy should climb as width grows and then level off. The claim fails if the curve is flat across widths or if the optimizer settings move accuracy more than the width does.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Linearized dynamics of implication transfer to new subjects
PROPOSAL: Analyse a one-layer linearized transformer trained by gradient descent on triples (s, r, a) and derive when a gradient step on a new subject's fact moves the output of relation r_2 toward the implied answer, through the direction shared by overlapping subjects. Verify the result on a four-layer nonlinear model, using subjects that appear in training only in the fact and recording the implication logit across steps.
CONTROLS: Compare predicted and measured implication logits for new subjects against the same model on subjects that appear only in the fact, against a copy with the shared direction removed by projection, and against a copy with the overlap fraction changed, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The derived transfer term should track the measured logit growth within a modest error across steps. The claim fails if the measured logit moves in the opposite direction or if the projection leaves it unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gradient analysis of implication logits on facts seen in training
PROPOSAL: Study a one-layer linearized transformer trained by gradient descent on triples (s, r, a) and work out how a step on a subject's fact shifts the output of relation r_2 toward the implied answer, as a function of the answer mapping that overlapping subjects share. Test this on a four-layer nonlinear model with subjects that were trained on both fact and implication, tracking the implication logit over training steps.
CONTROLS: Compare predicted and measured implication logits for trained subjects against the same model on subjects that appear with both fact and implication, against a copy with the shared direction removed by projection, and against a copy with the overlap fraction changed, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The derived transfer term should follow the measured logit growth within a modest error across steps. The claim fails if the measured logit moves in the opposite direction or if the projection leaves it unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint tracking of deduction and hallucination during injection
PROPOSAL: Inject 500 new subjects into a transformer pretrained on synthetic triples by fine-tuning on their facts only, then query two things at every 200 steps: the log-probability of the implied answer for each new subject, and the rate at which the model gives a confident but incorrect answer to a relation it never saw for that subject. Plot both against steps and test whether they rise together.
CONTROLS: Compare the implied-answer log-probability against the confident wrong-answer rate on the same new subjects, against the same measures on subjects whose facts were withheld from fine-tuning, and against the same measures after shuffled fact labels, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: The implied-answer log-probability and the confident wrong-answer rate should rise on the same steps. The claim fails if one rises while the other stays flat, or if both rise on the withheld subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fact memorization curves during injection
PROPOSAL: Inject 500 new subjects into a transformer pretrained on synthetic triples by fine-tuning on their facts only, then query two things at every 200 steps: the training loss on those facts, and the accuracy with which the model recalls each stated fact. Plot both against steps and test whether memorization saturates before the end of fine-tuning, noting the step at which each curve flattens.
CONTROLS: Compare the fact-recall accuracy against the training loss on the same new subjects, against the same measures on subjects whose facts were withheld from fine-tuning, and against the same measures after shuffled fact labels, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 30
PREDICTION: The fact-recall accuracy and the training loss should settle on the same steps. The claim fails if one keeps moving while the other stays flat, or if both improve on the withheld subjects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rule consistency as the condition for deduction on new subjects
PROPOSAL: Construct synthetic worlds in which the mapping from relation r_1 answers to relation r_2 answers is either a consistent rule or an arbitrary assignment per subject, with 1,000 subjects each. Train a four-layer transformer on each world with partial overlap between facts and implications, then measure accuracy on implications of subjects seen only in a fact and the size of the gap between the worlds.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy between the consistent-rule world and the arbitrary-assignment world with the same subjects and overlap, against a copy trained on the consistent rule with the relation labels renamed, and against a copy trained on twice the facts per subject, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Accuracy on new subjects should be far higher in the consistent-rule world, with the arbitrary world near chance. The claim fails if the two worlds differ by less than the seed spread or if renaming labels changes the result.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data scale and deduction on new subjects
PROPOSAL: Generate synthetic worlds that share one consistent mapping from relation r_1 answers to relation r_2 answers, and give them subject counts that grow fourfold across the worlds. Fit a transformer of four layers to every world using partial overlap between facts and implications; afterwards score implications of subjects seen only in a fact and compare worlds.
CONTROLS: Compare held-out implication accuracy between the smallest world and the largest world with the same relations and overlap, against a copy trained on the smaller world with the relation labels renamed, and against a copy trained on twice the facts per subject, each repeated with five seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Accuracy on new subjects should be higher in the larger world, with a modest gap. The claim fails if the two worlds differ by less than the seed spread or if renaming labels changes the result.
